source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 17 — ENOCH'S FIRST COSMIC TOUR — Aramaic 4Q204 1 viii preserves portions; Greek Akhmim 17:1-8 substantially complete; Ge'ez full. Cosmic-geography vocabulary (fiery mountains, river-of-fire, abyss/abussos) is central.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ παραλαβόντες με εἴς τινα τόπον ἤγαγον, ἐν ᾧ οἱ ὄντες ἐκεῖ γίνονται ὡς πῦρ φλεγόμενον, καὶ ὅταν θέλωσιν φαίνονται ὡς ἄνθρωποι.
verses.translit: Kai paralabontes me eis tina topon ēgagon, en hō hoi ontes ekei ginontai hōs pyr phlegomenon, kai hotan thelōsin phainontai hōs anthrōpoi.
verses.text_geez: ወነሥኡኒ፡ ወወሰዱኒ፡ ውስተ፡ መካን፡ ኀበ፡ እለ፡ ሀለዉ፡ ህየ፡ ይከውኑ፡ ከመ፡ እሳት፡ ዘይነድድ፡ ወሶበ፡ ፈቀዱ፡ ይትዐየኑ፡ ከመ፡ ሰብእ፡
verses.notes: Opening of Enoch's first cosmic tour. The angelic guides take Enoch to a place where the inhabitants appear as flaming fire but can take human form at will. The shape-shifting motif resonates with Gen 18-19 (the three visitors to Abraham appearing as men), Jdg 13 (the angel of YHWH appearing to Manoah), and later Hekhalot angelology.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἤγαγόν με εἰς τόπον σκοτεινόν, καὶ εἰς ὄρος, οὗ ἡ κεφαλὴ ἀφικνεῖτο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: Kai ēgagon me eis topon skoteinon, kai eis oros, hou hē kephalē aphikneito eis ton ouranon.
verses.text_geez: ወወሰዱኒ፡ ውስተ፡ መካን፡ ጽልመታዊ፡ ወውስተ፡ ደብር፡ ዘርእሱ፡ ይበጽሕ፡ ውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.notes: The cosmic mountain whose summit reaches heaven. Cross-corpus to the axis-mundi motif: Mt Hermon, Mt Sapunu (Ugaritic), Mt Olympus, Mt Meru, the Mesopotamian Ekur. The phrase 'head reaches heaven' echoes Gen 11:4 (Babel-tower) inversely — here it is a divinely-shown cosmic landmark, not a transgressive human construction.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶδον τόπους τῶν φωστήρων καὶ τοὺς θησαυροὺς τῶν ἀστέρων καὶ τῶν βροντῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ ἀκρότατα τοῦ ἀβύσσου, ὅπου τόξον πυρὸς καὶ τὰ βέλη αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ θήκη αὐτῶν, καὶ πᾶσαι αἱ ἀστραπαί.
verses.translit: Kai eidon topous tōn phōstērōn kai tous thēsaurous tōn asterōn kai tōn brontōn, kai eis ta akrotata tou abyssou, hopou toxon pyros kai ta belē autōn kai hē thēkē autōn, kai pasai hai astrapai.
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ መካናተ፡ ብርሃናት፡ ወመዛግብተ፡ ከዋክብት፡ ወመባርቅት፡ ወውስተ፡ አጽናፈ፡ ቀላይ፡ ኀበ፡ ቀስተ፡ እሳት፡ ወአሕጻቲሁ፡ ወከዓቦቱ፡ ወኵሉ፡ መባርቅት፡
verses.notes: The 'storehouses' (θησαυροί / መዛግብት) of stars, thunders, and lightning. Cross-corpus: Job 38:22 (storehouses of snow and hail); Jer 10:13 (Yahweh brings out wind from his storehouses); cf. 1 En 41:3-5; 60:11-22 (the Similitudes' elaborated meteorological-storehouse cosmology). The bow-of-fire and arrows recall the divine warrior in Hab 3:9-11.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἤγαγόν με μέχρι τοῦ ζοφώδους ὕδατος καὶ μέχρι τοῦ πυρὸς τῆς δύσεως, τὸ προσδεχόμενον πάντας τοὺς φωστῆρας τοῦ ἡλίου.
verses.translit: Kai ēgagon me mechri tou zophōdous hydatos kai mechri tou pyros tēs dyseōs, to prosdechomenon pantas tous phōstēras tou hēliou.
verses.text_geez: ወወሰዱኒ፡ እስከ፡ ማይ፡ ጽልመታዊ፡ ወእስከ፡ እሳት፡ ዘዐረብ፡ ዘይትዌከፍ፡ ኵሎ፡ ብርሃናተ፡ ፀሐይ፡
verses.notes: The 'fire of the West' that receives the sun. Cosmological-myth-pattern: the sun is swallowed by the western waters / fire at sunset. Cross-corpus: Egyptian Re entering Duat through the western horizon; Mesopotamian Shamash entering the gate-of-the-mountain of sunset; Ps 19:5-6 (the sun's tabernacle and circuit).

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἦλθον ἐπὶ ποταμὸν πυρός, οὗ τὸ πῦρ ῥεῖ ὡς ὕδωρ, καὶ ἐκχεῖται εἰς θάλασσαν μεγάλην πρὸς δυσμάς.
verses.translit: Kai ēlthon epi potamon pyros, hou to pyr rhei hōs hydōr, kai ekcheitai eis thalassan megalēn pros dysmas.
verses.text_geez: ወመጻእኩ፡ ኀበ፡ ተከዜ፡ እሳት፡ ዘይውኅዝ፡ እሳቱ፡ ከመ፡ ማይ፡ ወይክዐው፡ ውስተ፡ ባሕር፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዘመንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡
verses.notes: **River of fire (potamos pyros) flowing to the western sea.** Cross-corpus DIRECT: Dan 7:10 'a stream of fire issued and came forth from before him'; cf. 1 En 14:19. Greco-Roman parallel: the Pyriphlegethon, one of the rivers of Hades (Hom. Od. 10.513, Plato Phaedo 113b). The river-of-fire as eschatological boundary becomes a major motif in later apocalyptic + patristic literature.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ποταμοὺς τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ ἕως τοῦ μεγάλου ποταμοῦ καὶ ἕως τοῦ μεγάλου σκότους ἤγγισα, καὶ ἀπῆλθον ὅπου πᾶσα σὰρξ οὐ περιπατεῖ.
verses.translit: Kai eidon tous potamous tous megalous, kai heōs tou megalou potamou kai heōs tou megalou skotous ēngisa, kai apēlthon hopou pasa sarx ou peripatei.
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ አፍላገ፡ ዐበይተ፡ ወእስከ፡ ተከዜ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ወእስከ፡ ጽልመት፡ ዐቢይ፡ ቀረብኩ፡ ወሖርኩ፡ ኀበ፡ ኵሉ፡ ዘሥጋ፡ ኢየሐውር፡
verses.notes: The great rivers and the great darkness — boundary-region where no flesh walks. Echoes Job 38:16-17 (the gates of death and deep darkness).

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶδον τὰ ὄρη τοῦ σκότους τοῦ χειμῶνος καὶ τὸν τόπον οὗ ἐκχεῖται πᾶν τὸ ὕδωρ τῆς ἀβύσσου.
verses.translit: Kai eidon ta orē tou skotous tou cheimōnos kai ton topon hou ekcheitai pan to hydōr tēs abyssou.
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ አድባረ፡ ጽልመቱ፡ ለክረምት፡ ወመካነ፡ ኀበ፡ ይክዐው፡ ኵሉ፡ ማይ፡ ዘቀላይ፡
verses.notes: Mountains of winter-darkness and the source of the cosmic waters of the **abyss (abussos / qalāy)**. Cross-corpus: Gen 1:2 (təhōm); Gen 7:11 (the fountains of the great deep burst forth in the Flood); Ps 104:6; Rev 9:1-2 (the abussos with key).

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶδον τὸ στόμα πάντων τῶν ποταμῶν τῆς γῆς καὶ τὸ στόμα τῆς ἀβύσσου.
verses.translit: Kai eidon to stoma pantōn tōn potamōn tēs gēs kai to stoma tēs abyssou.
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ አፈ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ አፍላገ፡ ምድር፡ ወአፈ፡ ቀላይ፡
verses.notes: The 'mouth' of all earthly rivers and of the cosmic abyss — the cosmic source-point. Echoes Mesopotamian Apsû (the freshwater abyss). The abussos lexeme links forward to NT eschatology (Rev 9, 11, 20).
